text.text: The job board for a residential builder or remodeler: every job with its contract, permit and schedule, the subcontractors booked on each phase, change orders signed before the work, and the punch list that gets you to final payment.

This workspace runs the office side of a building company: what is sold, what is being built, who is on site this week, what the owner still has to sign, and what stands between you and the final payment. Your estimating and accounting software stay where they are; this is where the job lives day to day.

text.text: The Mbeki bath is cost plus. The plumber found a drain with the wrong slope behind the wall, so a change order for the rework went to the owner with three days added. The supply and drain phase failed inspection and shows Delayed until the change is signed and the fix is re-inspected.
The first two weeks of a job decide whether it finishes on time and on budget. Every start follows the same order so nothing depends on memory.
Contract signed and the deposit received. Enter both on the project and set
Permit applied for. Put the number in
at Applied until the card is in hand. No work that needs a permit starts before it is Issued.
Selections confirmed in writing: fixtures, finishes, windows, anything with a lead time. Order long-lead items now.
Phases added for the whole job with rough dates, and the first three weeks booked with real subs.
Every sub on the job checked: insurance not expired, license number recorded, W-9 on file.
Meet the owner on site with the superintendent. Cover:
Working hours, parking, the bathroom the crew may use, and where materials are stored
Which rooms are off limits and how the house is protected (floor covering, dust walls)
Who the owner calls with questions; one name only
How change orders work: priced and signed before the work, no exceptions
The payment schedule from the contract
Permit card posted where the inspector can see it.
Photos of existing conditions in every room you will touch, especially floors, walls and anything already damaged.
Dust protection up before the first cut.

Build the phases in the order the trades need each other: demolition, framing, rough plumbing, rough electrical and heating, rough inspection, insulation, drywall, finishes, final inspection. Each inspection is marked on the phase that needs it. A failed inspection sets the phase to
until the fix is done and re-inspected.

The Tanaka-Wells roof is signed with the deposit in. The roofing permit is applied for, so the tear-off phase stays Not started and the inspection is marked To schedule. Highcrest Roofing's insurance has lapsed; they cannot be booked until a new certificate arrives.
Most disputes on finished jobs come from the first week: an unclear selection, a verbal change, or a damaged floor nobody photographed. A complete start costs an hour and saves days at the end.

A change order is any change to the price, the scope or the schedule of a signed contract. Unsigned changes are the most common way a profitable job turns into a loss, and the most common reason owners stop trusting a builder.
No changed work starts until the owner has signed the change order. Not a text, not a nod on site: a signed document with a price and the days it adds.

Every sub on your site carries risk for you. If their insurance has lapsed and someone is hurt, your policy may end up paying. Paperwork first, then the schedule.

The punch list is the last few percent of the work and often the last few percent of your profit, because final payment and retainage wait on it. Finish it fast and finish it once.

Book a check-in call at 30 days and at 11 months, before the one-year warranty ends. Small fixes done quickly turn owners into referrals.

The Ashgrove basement has three open items: caulk in the shower, a scuffed baseboard by the bar and a cabinet door to align. The outlet cover is fixed but not yet checked. The final paint phase finishes this week, so the closeout walk is booked for Friday.
